text:
elaine: Heads-up — found a blob in a partner S3 object that looks like a KMS-wrapped ciphertext containing a service-account JSON. Putting initial details here so we can triage quickly. :rotating_light:

sanjay: Path? sample snippet? Is it public? :eyes:

elaine: s3://partner-prod-logs/ingest/2026-03-20/ingest.log
Here's the trailing lines I pulled (redacted):
```
...INFO payload: eyJhbGciOiJraWQiLCJ0eXAiOiJKV1QifQ... (base64 blob)
```
Object ACL is private but the partner recently ran a bucket-policy change. Not sure when it was exposed.

jules-oncall: tagging oncall — @jules-oncall stepping in. Do we know whose KMS key wrapped it?

elaine: The ciphertext metadata includes ARN: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:999999:key/abcd-ef01. That account != ours. So partner-side KMS. But the decrypted plaintext looks like a GCP service account JSON we previously shared for integration (redacted).

leo: Ok — threat: if partner KMS policy is lax or a partner employee exfiltrated logs, our SA key could be used. Short plan: contain + rotate creds + audit.

sanjay: Agreed. Immediate asks: 1) search for other occurrences across partner buckets (I can kick that off). 2) Rotate the SA and revoke existing keys. 3) Update partner with new short-lived key/role. 4) Ensure Vault/our transit keys are not involved.

elaine: I already told partner-ops channel (DMed them) and asked for an audit of who accessed that object in the partner account.

leo: Minimal rotation commands (GCP) — run from a secure environment: 
```
gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=sa-integration@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable <KEY_ID> --iam-account=sa-integration@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create --iam-account=sa-integration@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --key-file-type=json new-sa-key.json
```
After creating new key: upload to Vault at path `secret/partners/partner-x/sa-integration` and give partner a short-lived signed token (prefer workload identity or short-lived OAuth).

jules-oncall: Also checklist for this incident: 
- Confirm SA email(s) that match plaintext (elaine)
- Revoke all keys for those SA(s) (leo)
- Rotate any Vault entries referencing that SA and increase audit retention to 90d on those paths (sanjay + security)
- Ask partner to rotate their KMS key or rekey and provide access audit (partner ops)
- Run repo/CI scan for embedded SA JSON (sanjay)

elaine: Quick note on Vault vs KMS concerns: if partner used our Vault-stored key material to provision the SA (via an integration) we need to confirm whether any Vault transit keys were used to sign or encrypt the artifact. If so, we may need to rewrap transit keys.

leo: Good point. I'll audit Vault audit-logs for `secret/partners/partner-x` and `transit/` entries in the last 30 days. If we see `rewrap` or `encrypt` calls that correspond, we'll escalate to key rewrap.

security-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0319. PagerDuty alerted to oncall. Priority: P2 (credential leak targeting partner logs). Links: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0319

sanjay: I'm running an S3 grep across partner buckets for similar base64-looking lines and KMS metadata. Posting results in ~20m.

jules-oncall: Owners: ela: liaison to partner, sanjay: search + CI scan, leo: revoke + Vault audit, me (jules): incident lead and coord.

elaine: I'll prepare the minimal disclosure to partner-ops: we've requested immediate ACL/history and asked them to hold from deleting the object until we snapshot it.

sanjay: If partner can't provide a short-lived integration, we should move them to workload-identity and delete static keys.

leo: After revoke, issue short-lived signed service account tokens or use workload identity federation. Also rotate any downstream service tokens that used the SA.

elaine: Final-ish: I'll attach the redacted snippet and timeline to the incident. If anyone finds more objects, drop them here. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
